Elaine (sales): Heads up — NovusBank just escalated to their C-suite. CISO says POC can't proceed without exec signoff unless we confirm BYOK KMS architecture + data egress control. They want an exec touchpoint tomorrow 10:00am PST. Can we get an internal unblock plan? @Anita (security) @Mike (legal) @Josh (eng-runtime) :urgent:
Anita (security): :wave: I saw the questionnaire. Key asks: BYOK attestation, key lifecycle (wrap/unwrap), and confirmation that no customer data leaves EU region during processing. We can provide architecture + threat model but need engineering to confirm KMS integration pattern.
Josh (eng-runtime): Quick note — our hosted path currently supports KMS-proxy for BYOK via wrapped keys in vault. Latency impact ~5–10ms per token for key fetch on cold start, negligible afterwards. I can sketch the flow.
Priya (product): For execs, they want a clear decision matrix: hosted w/ BYOK vs Dedicated vs Private. We should show risk tradeoffs and timelines. I can assemble a 1-pager if we agree on bullets.
Mike (legal): I'll pull the SOC2 artifact and previous KMS attestation redactions. Also need to confirm contract language for key custody — is customer allowed to rotate frequently? Need input from eng on rotation API.
Leo (sales-ops): Logistics — NovusBank wants a recorded bridge + slide deck. They've asked for a FedRAMP-ish control mapping even though not required. Can we reuse the 'enterprise-security-mapping' deck?
deploy-bot: runbook created: /runbooks/novusbank-poc-escalation-1718076543 — assigned to @Josh, @Anita, @Mike
Anita (security): I'll draft the threat-model bullet list. Josh — can you confirm whether keys are ever exported from our HSMs? Need explicit 'no-export' language for the deck.
Josh (eng-runtime): Confirmed: keys are never exported in plaintext. We do key wrapping with customer KEK, our service stores wrapped DEKs. I can paste minimal flow: ```1) Client uploads wrapped DEK via KMS-proxy 2) Wrapped DEK stored in encrypted store 3) Runtime unwraps in-memory to decrypt model cache only during inference``` That should be safe to show.
Mike (legal): Good. I'll draft a contract clause: "Customer-managed KEK: Redwood will accept wrapped data encryption keys and will not export KEKs or unwrapped DEKs except per lawful process." Will circulate for review.
Elaine (sales): Team — NovusBank exec asked: can we promise no egress outside EU for PII? Anita/Josh, what's the firm answer? We need a one-line for the exec: yes/no + mitigation.
Anita (security): Short answer: Yes — for Dedicated and Private we can guarantee processing within EU. For Hosted, we can *route* to EU region but shared infra means additional controls and contract language required. I'll write the exact phrasing.
Josh (eng-runtime): I'll validate infra routing config and cert that their POC traffic can be pinned to eu-west-1 nodes. Also will list fallback behaviors if failover triggers (we can set policy to prefer EU-only, but full hard guarantee requires Dedicated/Private).
Priya (product): I'll turn the above into a single slide: architecture diagram (with wrapped-key flow), one-liner on egress, timeline for Dedicated vs Hosted (days vs weeks), and suggested ask for execs.
Leo (sales-ops): Can someone drop the deck in this thread when ready? NovusBank wants final slide deck by EOD today so they can prep internal invite.
Josh (eng-runtime): Will drop a minimal architecture SVG + sequence snippet in 45m.
Anita (security): I'll attach the threat-model bullets + recommended mitigations in 1hr.
Mike (legal): I'll post the draft contract clause and redlines in 2hr.
Elaine (sales): Fantastic. I'll schedule the bridge for 10:00am PST and send invite once deck lands. For now — assign owners: Anita (security) deck bullets, Josh (arch diagram + infra cert), Mike (contract clause), Priya (slide assembly), Leo (deck QA + invite).
Priya (product): Noted. I'll assemble and push to the runbook path.
Elaine (sales): Thanks all — please ping here when you've uploaded assets. :pray:
